title: continuous-json-safety-truncation-retries-procedures
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: Streaming LLM responses that encode structured JSON objects can be truncated mid-object, contain escaped characters that are interpreted differently by downstream tools, or be retransmitted on retry leading to duplicate partial objects. This ticket defines a pragmatic, backward-compatible set of procedures for the Redwood API and SDKs to: (1) preserve structured output semantics for consumers (including function/tool callers), (2) minimize latency and cost regressions, and (3) enable safe retries and resumptions across client and server implementations.
background: We have sporadic customer reports where streaming responses used for tool calling or JSON ingestion either fail JSON parsing on the client, produce duplicated partial objects after network retries, or lose critical escape sequences (e.g., embedded JSON strings, backslashes). Existing tickets touch on framing and resume but don't cover a complete, deployable procedure that balances latency and correctness across hosted, dedicated, and Private deployments. This work intends to standardize the approach so SDKs and server-side routers implement interoperable semantics.
goals: Define a simple framing layer that enables clients to detect object boundaries even when truncated
Specify escaping and canonicalization rules so tool callers and structured-output consumers see deterministic strings
Provide a retry/resume protocol that avoids duplicate partial object emission in common failure modes
Document SDK behavior (JS, Python, Go) and server-side toggles to gradually roll out the change
non_goals: Redesigning the entire streaming protocol (keep changes additive and backward-compatible)
Enforcing a single canonical JSON serializer for all models (we provide guidance and normalization)
proposed_solution_summary: Add a lightweight control-channel envelope to streaming responses: emit newline-prefixed control records and JSON payload frames. Control records indicate object start, object end, and escaped-literal markers. On truncation, include a final 'incomplete' control record with an idempotency token so clients can request a resume or safe retry. SDKs will provide a 'reconcile_stream' helper that stitches frames and applies canonical unescaping rules before handing finalized objects to the caller.
detailed_spec:
Framing: Each stream chunk is UTF-8. There are two line types separated by '
': CONTROL:<base64-json> and PAYLOAD:<utf8-json-fragment>. CONTROL lines are small JSON metadata blobs encoded in base64 to avoid interfering with payload slicing. PAYLOAD lines are partial UTF-8 substrings of the model's emitted JSON representation.

Control field set: {event: 'obj_start'|'obj_end'|'incomplete'|'keepalive', obj_id: string, seq: int, token: string (opaque idempotency)} encoded as compact JSON then base64. Example CONTROL:eyJldmVudCI6Im9iX3N0YXJ0Iiwi....

Object assembly: Clients buffer PAYLOAD fragments by obj_id/seq. receipt of CONTROL 'obj_end' signals assembly complete and client attempts JSON.parse on the concatenated payload after running the canonical unescape step. If parsing fails, client marks the object as 'malformed' and includes full raw payload in telemetry while returning an error to the application only if configured to be strict.

Escaping rules: SDKs apply two canonical passes before delivery: (1) normalize all backslash sequences to valid JSON escapes (
, 	, ", \) and convert lone control characters into unicode escape points; (2) collapse repeated escapes introduced by nested model stringification (e.g., stringified JSON embedded as a string) into a single canonical level unless the schema indicates a raw string field. Document a configurable flag 'preserve_raw_strings' for advanced callers.

Truncation semantics: When server detects imminent truncation (stream closed or token limit reached) it emits a CONTROL 'incomplete' with obj_id and token. The server must include a short diagnostic 'reason' value. Clients can choose: (a) request server-side resume via the token within a short window, (b) treat the object as failed, or (c) attempt best-effort repair if allowed by policy. Resume requests are routed to the same model/version where possible but may be served by a compatible variant; token encodes compatibility hints.

Retry idempotency: All emitted objects include obj_id and token. On client reconnect or retry, SDKs send the last-seen token; server performs delta-merge and avoids re-emitting already acknowledged seq numbers. If server cannot resume reliably, it will respond with CONTROL 'cannot_resume' and a suggested fallback: full non-streaming generation for the object.

Function/tool calling compatibility: For streams used as direct inputs to tool calls, the SDK will expose an option 'deliver_partial_to_tool' (default: false). If true, assembled partial but syntactically valid objects are forwarded to the tool; otherwise only finalized objects are forwarded. The server-side will annotate control events with 'intended_as_tool' hint to help routing and replay decisions.

Backward compatibility: If a client does not understand CONTROL records, it will see them as leading lines and should ignore CONTROL:<...> prefixes; PAYLOAD lines remain plain JSON fragments so basic concatenation still yields the original bytes in older SDKs (best-effort). Documentation will recommend SDK upgrades for production use cases requiring resume and deduplication.
acceptance_criteria: SDKs (JS + Python) implement the framing parser and expose 'reconcile_stream' with the canonicalization and resume APIs
Server emits CONTROL records for at least 90% of truncated streams in staging traffic after rollout toggle enabled
End-to-end test harness shows no more than 1% of previously failing truncated-object cases (repro script) failing after changes
Compatibility test: legacy client that ignores CONTROL lines can still reconstruct the same full JSON blobs when no truncation occurs
Telemetry: 'stream_incomplete' and 'stream_resume_success' events are available in Console and tagged by obj_id and model_version
implementation_notes: Server: add control-event generation in the response emitter layer. Toggle behind 'streaming-control-frames' runtime flag (per-tenant).
Router: ensure tokens are opaque but include model_version and short checksum in the payload to validate resume compatibility without exposing internals.

JS SDK: streaming client returns an async iterator of {type: 'control'|'payload', data: string} and provides reconcileStream(iterator, opts) helper. Provide migration guide for existing streaming APIs.
Python SDK: expose StreamingFrame class and helper function stitch_frames(...). Ensure sync and async client parity.
Logging: redact token in logs; surface only token suffix in debug views.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (canary): enable flag for internal tenants and run synthetic truncation tests (1 week)
Phase 1: opt-in on-staging for customers with active SDK upgrades (2 weeks)
Phase 2: gradual 10% ramp on hosted API with server-side toggle (1 week), monitor malformed JSON and resume success rates
Phase 3: full rollout when resume_success >= 95% and no customer regression reports (monitor for 2 weeks)
Rollback: server toggle off returns to previous behavior; SDKs continue to be compatible with legacy streams
test_plan: Unit: parser edgecases for partial unicode codepoints across payload fragments
Integration: simulated network drop during object emission, assert resume behavior with token exchange
Fuzz: random escape sequences and nested JSON-in-string scenarios to verify canonicalization does not corrupt content
Load: ensure control frames add <2% CPU and negligible latency under normal traffic patterns
telemetry_and_alerting: SLO/Alert: page on stream_resume_success_rate < 90% for 15m, or malformed_after_assembly_rate spike > 0.5%
Dashboards: per-model and per-tenant breakdown of incomplete vs completed objects
